# stable_id|category|genres|premise

wd-p-0477|accountability|realist,political|A city opens an apology office that can acknowledge harm but authorize no compensation. Its clerk receives a claim asking only for an acknowledgment that would automatically trigger compensation under a different department's rules.

wd-p-0478|coordination|realist,satire|A committee creates a second committee to reduce meeting time. The new body's first decision requires consultation with every member of the original, and the secretary is the only person authorized to cancel either meeting.

wd-p-0479|access|realist,political|A public agency moves all applications online after recording few requests for paper forms. A receptionist knows that people unable to use the website have also been unable to submit the requests used to justify the change.

wd-p-0480|credit|realist,satire|A company rewards employees for proposing improvements but deducts time spent implementing them from performance scores. A worker wins the prize and is placed on a disciplinary plan in the same announcement.

wd-p-0481|consent|realist,political|A neighborhood survey reports unanimous support because nonresponses were counted as agreement. The organizer tries to collect explicit answers and finds that the promised project has already begun using the supposed consensus as its permit.

wd-p-0482|measurement|realist,satire|A museum measures visitor engagement by time spent in each room. A faulty door makes an unpopular exhibit the most successful, and repairing it threatens the curator whose funding depends on the new figures.

wd-p-0483|obligation|realist,political|A public contractor must hire local workers, but the approved residency documents exclude people displaced by the project. A recruiter can meet the numerical target only by overlooking the people the condition was intended to benefit.

wd-p-0484|trust|realist,satire|A company introduces anonymous feedback with prizes for the most useful suggestion. An employee's winning complaint can be rewarded only if she identifies herself to the manager whose conduct it describes.

wd-p-0485|resources|realist,political|A council allocates repair funds to streets with the most reported potholes. Residents of an unpaved street must explain that having no potholes is not evidence that their road is in better condition.

wd-p-0486|expertise|realist,satire|An efficiency consultant eliminates a receptionist's apparently redundant conversations. The office then loses the informal information that made every formal appointment run on time, and rehiring the receptionist requires admitting the report measured the wrong work.

wd-p-0487|accountability|realist,political|A regulator discovers that a company has complied with the letter of every safety recommendation by changing job titles. The hazardous tasks remain, but no employee is officially assigned the role to which the rules apply.

wd-p-0488|coordination|realist,satire|A shared office introduces a booking system for quiet rooms. Employees reserve rooms to escape the booking meetings, and the administrator must decide whether the resulting empty desks prove success or failure.

wd-p-0489|access|realist,political|A city makes public comments available only as scanned images. A resident requests searchable text and is asked to identify the inaccessible passages she cannot search well enough to locate.

wd-p-0490|credit|realist,political|A volunteer translation team asks to be named in a public report. The agency agrees only if they accept responsibility for a summary edited by officials who removed their warnings about ambiguous wording.

wd-p-0491|consent|realist,satire|An employer asks staff to choose a voluntary social event, then records abstention as an absence from team activities. The employee appointed to increase participation realizes that the survey cannot register a wish for no event.

wd-p-0492|measurement|realist,political|A school celebrates reduced exclusions after renaming them temporary placements. A counselor discovers that the supposedly placed pupils receive no instruction, and restoring their official status would make the school's headline achievement disappear.

wd-p-0493|obligation|realist,satire|A workplace assigns every task an owner to improve accountability. The system cannot assign shared work, so colleagues begin doing favors outside the records while the manager praises the apparent elimination of collaboration.

wd-p-0494|trust|realist,political|A city releases anonymized service records to demonstrate fairness. A local researcher recognizes herself from a unique sequence of appointments and must expose the privacy failure without exposing the other residents she can also identify.

wd-p-0495|resources|realist,satire|A public office receives funding to modernize its waiting room but none to shorten waiting times. A clerk proposes transparent displays, only to discover that the approved design hides the queue length from everyone outside the room.

wd-p-0496|expertise|realist,political|A planning board invites a resident as a community expert, then refuses to reimburse the work because she lacks professional credentials. She can accept an honorary title, but the title would require her to speak for neighbors who chose nobody to represent them.

wd-p-0497|accountability|realist,satire|A manager requires every error to have a named cause. A team invents a fictional employee for faults caused by conflicting instructions, and the fictional worker is selected for a performance-improvement award.

wd-p-0498|coordination|realist,political|Two public agencies each provide transport only after the other confirms an appointment. A caseworker can break the loop by making an unauthorized booking, but its cancellation fee will be charged to the applicant if either agency refuses.

wd-p-0499|access|realist,satire|A library bans handwritten signs to maintain a welcoming professional appearance. The official sign-ordering system then fails, leaving staff unable to explain that the closed door is broken rather than a new restriction.

wd-p-0500|credit|realist,political|A research institution names a discovery after the principal investigator. The technician credited only in acknowledgments owns the notebook establishing the result and wants correction without having her years of uncredited routine work reduced to one heroic moment.

wd-p-0501|consent|realist,political|A community land agreement allows withdrawal only before construction begins. Residents learn that preliminary fencing counted as construction before the consultation meeting, making a promised choice expire before it was presented.

wd-p-0502|measurement|realist,satire|A company ranks branches by customer complaints. One branch improves by making the complaint form harder to find, and the employee sent to teach its successful method is the person who originally designed an accessible alternative.

wd-p-0503|obligation|realist,political|A town accepts a gift that requires maintaining a monument forever. Decades later, the upkeep consumes the public space budget, and the donor's descendants offer release only if the town renames the park after another family member.

wd-p-0504|trust|realist,satire|An office introduces a rule that every instruction must be written. Informal requests continue as friendly questions, and an employee's refusal to infer an order is recorded as poor communication.

wd-p-0505|resources|realist,political|A water board charges less for high-volume use to encourage efficient infrastructure. A cooperative proves that several small households together use more than the threshold, but pooling their meters would transfer responsibility for every unpaid bill to the group.

wd-p-0506|expertise|realist,satire|A training course teaches staff to sound confident when uncertain. The instructor's own emergency warning is dismissed because she carefully states its limits, and solving the crisis requires making uncertainty sound credible again.

wd-p-0507|accountability|realist,political|A redevelopment contract protects existing shops but defines a shop as a registered leaseholder. The market's stallholders can qualify only by signing leases with the developer whose project threatens them.

wd-p-0508|coordination|realist,satire|A company installs a system that automatically declines conflicting meetings. Two departments keep moving their meetings in response until the system reserves every hour of the only worker who belongs to both.

wd-p-0509|access|realist,political|A court offers free interpretation only after a person requests it in the court's official language. A volunteer demonstrates the barrier and is asked to complete the requests on everyone's behalf without being allowed to explain their cases.

wd-p-0510|credit|realist,satire|A manager asks staff to write their own praise for an annual report. One writes an exact description of invisible maintenance work, and the manager requests more inspiring language that would make the work unrecognizable.

wd-p-0511|consent|realist,political|A school obtains blanket permission for educational photographs. A parent discovers that a child's image is being used to advertise a policy the family has challenged, and the school treats removal as withdrawing the child from ordinary classroom activities.

wd-p-0512|measurement|realist,political|A hospital's appointment target rewards short visits. A clinician finds that patients needing interpreters appear less efficient even when their actual medical consultation is brief, and correcting the measure would expose years of unequal scheduling.

wd-p-0513|obligation|realist,satire|A workplace makes every employee responsible for welcoming newcomers. Each assumes someone else has provided essential instructions, and a new hire discovers that everyone praises the onboarding process without knowing who performs it.

wd-p-0514|trust|realist,political|A city launches a confidential reporting line staffed by employees temporarily transferred from the offices being reported. The supervisor can improve independence only by hiring people whom the budget's eligibility rules exclude.

wd-p-0515|resources|realist,satire|A committee buys software to reduce paperwork, then prints every digital approval for audit. The clerk who proposes stopping the prints must supply a paper form explaining where the paper records will be stored after they cease to exist.

wd-p-0516|expertise|realist,political|A building inspector uses local residents' observations to identify a hidden hazard. The formal report cannot cite anonymous knowledge, but naming the residents would expose unauthorized alterations they made to stay safe before officials responded.

wd-p-0517|accountability|realist,satire|An institution promises to implement every recommendation in an external review. It creates a recommendation-tracking office whose first request is permission to decide which recommendations count as recommendations.

wd-p-0518|coordination|realist,political|A city's emergency shelters each assume another site will accept people with pets. An organizer finds no actual destination and must decide whether to break the rule at her own already crowded shelter.

wd-p-0519|access|realist,satire|A public building installs a help kiosk to replace its information desk. The kiosk directs anyone needing personal assistance to the location of the former desk, which is now a locked equipment cupboard.

wd-p-0520|credit|realist,political|An archive celebrates a major donation but omits the volunteers who prevented its destruction. They can obtain recognition only by revealing that the donor had ordered the material discarded before changing his mind.

wd-p-0521|consent|realist,satire|A committee votes to require unanimous agreement on future decisions. The sole dissenter is told that disagreement cannot be recorded because the new rule has already passed by the majority she opposed.

wd-p-0522|measurement|realist,political|A housing office counts every offered property as a successful placement. A resident receives repeated offers she cannot access, and accepting one for the sake of the statistics would end the assistance she still needs.

wd-p-0523|obligation|realist,political|A neighborhood signs an agreement to maintain a public garden in exchange for use of the land. The city later interprets maintenance to include an expensive retaining wall whose failure predates the garden.

wd-p-0524|trust|realist,satire|A company asks staff to recommend friends for jobs while keeping applications confidential. An employee receives a rejection addressed to the friend she never recommended, revealing that the referral system inferred a relationship from private calendar entries.

wd-p-0525|resources|realist,political|A relief fund reimburses costs only after receipts are submitted. A volunteer finds that the families with no money to spend first are absent from the accounts used to show the program's universal reach.

wd-p-0526|expertise|realist,satire|A workshop invites a repair expert to demonstrate a simple fix. The sponsor supplies a sealed product designed not to be repaired, and the expert's honest demonstration would consist of showing why the promised method cannot work.

wd-p-0527|accountability|realist,political|A public consultation removes repeated submissions as duplicates. A resident discovers that coordinated opposition is being counted once while individually worded support is counted separately, and the appeal process treats the counting rule as already settled.

wd-p-0528|coordination|realist,satire|An office introduces flexible seating but requires every employee to list a fixed desk for emergency planning. The administrator assigns fictional desks, which the evacuation drill then treats as occupied locations requiring search.

wd-p-0529|access|realist,political|A transport service permits companions only when essential. A passenger can travel independently on the route but cannot safely reach its isolated pickup point, a need the assessment excludes because it occurs before boarding.

wd-p-0530|credit|realist,satire|A company announces that a successful product was created by everyone equally. The equal credit prevents the low-paid designer from documenting the specific work needed for a professional qualification, while senior staff use the product in their portfolios.

wd-p-0531|consent|realist,political|A council records attendance at a meeting as participation in designing a policy. A resident who attended only to object finds her photograph in a display presenting the policy as community-created.

wd-p-0532|measurement|realist,satire|A performance system measures response speed but not resolution. An employee automates immediate acknowledgments, wins recognition, and is asked to teach colleagues a practice that has made genuine replies harder to distinguish from empty ones.

wd-p-0533|obligation|realist,political|A town's snow-clearing agreement assigns residents the path outside their homes. A corner-house resident faces four times the work, and asking for a fairer share reveals that the original rule was negotiated before the street was extended.

wd-p-0534|trust|realist,satire|An institution claims no complaints were received during a difficult transition. The person preparing the report discovers that every complaint was logged as a request for information and answered with the same transition announcement.

wd-p-0535|resources|realist,political|A municipal grant requires applicants to show matching volunteer hours. A caregiver's unpaid work qualifies in principle, but counting it would imply that the public service it substitutes for has been delivered at no cost.

wd-p-0536|expertise|realist,satire|A company hires a specialist to simplify its language. The specialist's first recommendation removes the phrase used to describe the job itself, making the contract appear to cover an undefined service.

wd-p-0537|accountability|realist,political|A regulator allows a dangerous machine to remain in service until a replacement is available. The owner keeps canceling replacement orders, using the continuing lack of availability as evidence that the exception still applies.

wd-p-0538|coordination|realist,satire|A workplace creates a shared calendar for uninterrupted work. Every manager books over the protected periods because the calendar marks employees as free of meetings, and the coordinator must explain why availability is not permission.

wd-p-0539|access|realist,political|A public hearing permits questions only about documents released in advance. The key appendix arrives late, and the chair argues that its contents cannot be discussed because no questions about it were submitted on time.

wd-p-0540|credit|realist,satire|A prize requires a personal account of overcoming adversity. An applicant writes about collective help and is asked to remove the helpers so the story will sound sufficiently individual to qualify.

wd-p-0541|consent|realist,political|A clinic asks patients to consent to research while they wait for urgent care. A receptionist realizes that many believe refusal changes their place in the queue, but clarifying the choice would contradict the approved recruitment script.

wd-p-0542|measurement|realist,satire|A city rewards neighborhoods that reduce waste collections. One district removes bins, and the official sent to celebrate discovers that residents are carrying rubbish into the neighboring district whose performance now appears to be worsening.

wd-p-0543|obligation|realist,political|A developer promises replacement community space of equal floor area. The offered room meets the dimensions but has columns preventing the activities displaced from the original hall, and the contract defines equivalence only by size.

wd-p-0544|trust|realist,satire|A workplace's anonymous suggestion box is replaced with a transparent digital dashboard. Staff can now see every suggestion except those about the dashboard, which administrators classify as technical support requests rather than feedback.

wd-p-0545|resources|realist,political|A school funds equipment according to recorded extracurricular participation. The teacher with no equipment has no participants, and the funding officer asks for evidence of demand that the missing equipment makes impossible to gather.

wd-p-0546|expertise|realist,satire|A manager asks the office's informal mentor to document all her advice before retirement. Reading the draft reveals that many solutions require quietly ignoring policies the manager claims are essential to the office's success.

wd-p-0547|accountability|realist,political|A council offers compensation for a service interruption but requires proof of a failed transaction. Residents who knew the service was unavailable made no attempt, leaving the best-informed users unable to demonstrate the loss.

wd-p-0548|coordination|realist,satire|A committee assigns a backup for every responsibility. During a drill, everyone defers to their backup, and the person designated to resolve uncertainty is the only role for which no backup was assigned.

wd-p-0549|access|realist,political|A housing appeal must be submitted from the address being disputed. A resident already removed from the property can complete the form only by asking the new occupant to receive the decision on her behalf.

wd-p-0550|credit|realist,satire|A company labels a product handcrafted after workers finish defects left by its automated line. The worker asked to demonstrate the craft must either repeat the machine's mistake publicly or explain why the supposedly traditional step exists.

wd-p-0551|consent|realist,political|A local archive accepts family papers on condition that private material stay closed for a fixed period. A donor later asks to open only the letters defending her own conduct, while the replies remain protected by the original restriction.
